title: Define the first production release boundary
objective: Turn the canonical foundations, expression suite, navigation and Golden Homepage into one explicit production-release plan without silently promoting candidate dependencies, exposing unredacted proof media or creating a second source of design truth.

included: complete canonical and candidate dependency inventory for Golden Homepage 1.0.0
release inclusion, exclusion and promotion matrix
self-contained package manifest and version boundary
named future consumer interface without modifying that consumer
excluded: publishing or deploying a production website
modifying the separate technical Mez Systems repository
live routes, analytics, payments, authentication or availability

acceptance: every dependency is classified as canonical, candidate, generated, evidence-only or consumer-owned
candidate components are either routed to their own human promotion gates or excluded behind a stable interface
no unredacted operating-proof media is release-eligible
the package boundary is self-contained and names clean-install, update, rollback and version-visibility evidence

verification.passCondition: the release plan parses, every dependency has one authority class and every exclusion has an owning follow-up
CMP-05 and CMP-06 retain candidate status unless separate Olli decisions explicitly promote them
the plan cannot include raw operating-proof media and defines a redacted provenance-preserving payload

stopConditions: a candidate component would need production authority without its own recorded human decision
the release would contain unredacted operating-proof media
the task requires changes inside a consumer repository
the package cannot be made self-contained without an undeclared private dependency
notes: This task defines the release boundary; it does not assemble or publish the production release.

The first follow-up is TASK-PORT-02-HOMEPAGE-DEPENDENCY-GATES: one batched packet with separate CMP-05 and CMP-06 promotion or exclusion decisions, followed by isolated package assembly and then a named consumer integration.
Completed on 2026-07-28. The release plan records central decision-ledger drift as a production-assembly blocker rather than mutating governance inside PORT-01.
